children: shares rose 18% on Thursday as the data-storage company’s preliminary fiscal 2028 outlook topped expectations, following which Wall Street analysts raised their price targets.
Piper Sandler raised its price target to $162 from $133, while Evercore raised its target to $145 from $130.
Citi, JPMorgan, Needham, BofA Global Research, and Morgan Stanley all raised their price targets, with BofA setting the highest target at $180, up from $150.

"Pure's initial FY28 outlook implies an acceleration, is 16% above Street, and shows improving profitability. We continue to place Everpure in our top 5 picks given the shift towards all-flash across customer-types (especially for AI-infrastructure), product advantages and share gains in storage," said Piper Sandler.

Evercore said the fiscal 2028 outlook raised the earnings bar and increased its fiscal 2028 EPS estimate to $5.01 from $3.45. Piper Sandler said the outlook was about 16% above its previous expectations and pointed to continued growth in AI infrastructure and hyperscaler demand.

Everpure said it expects fiscal 2028 revenue of $7B to $7.3B, up 39% to 45% from the prior year. The outlook compares with analyst consensus of $6.37B. The company expects non-GAAP operating income of $1.7B to $1.9B, up 80% to 100%.
For fiscal 2027, Everpure reaffirmed revenue guidance of $5.03B to $5.07B, compared with analyst estimates of $5.05B.

three newer businesses—Modern Data Software, Scale AI and Hyperscale Solutions — are expected to account for about 20% of revenue by fiscal 2030. Its other growth areas include Core and Core AI, which cover its storage products and subscription services.

title: Wall Street raises Everpure targets after upbeat outlook
